entries.title: Psalms 89:1
segments: . Of Ethan--(See on

, title). This Psalm was composed during some season of great national distress, perhaps Absalom's rebellion. It contrasts the promised prosperity and perpetuity of David's throne (with reference to the great promise of

), with a time when God appeared to have forgotten His covenant. The picture thus drawn may typify the promises and the adversities of Christ's kingdom, and the terms of confiding appeal to God provided appropriate prayers for the divine aid and promised blessing. 
 
    1. mercies--those promised (

), and-- 
 
    faithfulness--that is, in fulfilling them.

segments: 2. I have said--expressed, as well as felt, my convictions (

segments: 3, 4. The object of this faith expressed in God's words (

segments: 6, 7. This is worthy of our belief, for His faithfulness (is praised) by the congregation of saints or holy ones; that is, angels (compare

). 
 
    sons of the mighty--(compare
). So is He to be admired on earth.

entries.title: Psalms 89:8
segments: 8-14. To illustrate His power and faithfulness examples are cited from history. His control of the sea (the most mighty and unstable object in nature), and of Egypt (

), the first great foe of Israel (subjected to utter helplessness from pride and insolence), are specimens. At the same time, the whole frame of nature founded and sustained by Him, Tabor and Hermon for "east and west," and "north and south," together representing the whole world, declare the same truth as to His attributes.

entries.title: Psalms 89:12
segments: 12. rejoice in thy name--praise Thy perfections by their very existence.

entries.title: Psalms 89:15
segments: 15. His government of righteousness is served by "mercy" and "truth" as ministers (

). 
 
    know the joyful sound--understand and appreciate the spiritual blessings symbolized by the feasts to which the people were called by the trumpet (

, &c.). 
 
    walk ... countenance--live in His favor (

16, 17. in--or, "by"

    glory--or, "beauty." 
 
    of their strength--They shall be adorned as well as protected. 
 
    our horn--exalt our power (

entries.title: Psalms 89:18
segments: 18. (Margin). Thus is introduced the promise to "our shield," "our king," David.

entries.title: Psalms 89:19
segments:
19-37. Then--when the covenant was established, of whose execution the exalted views of God now given furnish assurance. 
 
    thou ... to thy holy one--or godly saint, object of favor (
). Nathan is meant (

). 
 
    laid help--literally, "given help." David was chosen and then exalted.

entries.title: Psalms 89:25
segments: 25. hand [and] right hand--power (

). 
 
    sea, and ... rivers--limits of his empire (

entries.title: Psalms 89:26
segments: 26, 27. first-born--one who is chief, most beloved or distinguished (
). In God's sight and purposes he was the first among all monarchs, and specially so in his typical relation to Christ.

entries.title: Psalms 89:28
segments: 28-37. This relation is perpetual with David's descendants, as a whole typical in official position of his last greatest descendant. Hence though in personal relations any of them might be faithless and so punished, their typical relation shall continue. His oath confirms His promise, and the most enduring objects of earth and heaven illustrate its perpetual force (

entries.title: Psalms 89:35
segments: 35. Once--one thing (

entries.title: Psalms 89:37
segments: 37. It shall ... moon ... heaven--literally, "As the moon, and the witness in the sky is sure, that is, the moon."

entries.title: Psalms 89:38
segments:
38-52. present a striking contrast to these glowing promises, in mournful evidences of a loss of God's favor.

entries.title: Psalms 89:39
segments: 39. An insult to the "crown," as of divine origin, was a profanation.

entries.title: Psalms 89:40
segments: 40-45. The ruin is depicted under several figures--a vineyard whose broken "hedges," and "strongholds," whose ruins invite spoilers and invaders; a warrior, whose enemies are aided by God, and whose sword's "edge"--literally, "rock" or "strength" (
) is useless; and a youth prematurely old.

entries.title: Psalms 89:45
segments: 45. days of his youth--or, "youthful vigor," that is, of the royal line, or promised perpetual kingdom, under the figure of a man.

entries.title: Psalms 89:46
segments: 46. How long, &c.--(Compare

entries.title: Psalms 89:47
segments: 47. These expostulations are excited in view of the identity of the prosperity of this kingdom with the welfare of all mankind (
); for if such is the fate of this chosen royal line.

entries.title: Psalms 89:48
segments: 48. What man--literally, "strong man--shall live?" and, indeed, have not all men been made in vain, as to glorifying God?

entries.title: Psalms 89:49
segments: 49-51. The terms of expostulation are used in view of the actual appearance that God had forsaken His people and forgotten His promise, and the plea for aid is urged in view of the reproaches of His and His people's enemies (compare
